title: Payout Reconciliation Explainer
user: Small ecommerce operators and their bookkeepers who need to reconcile processor payouts against orders, refunds, fees, and bank deposits without opaque enterprise accounting tooling.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An ecommerce reconciliation builder asks businesses and accountants what is most frustrating about matching Shopify, payment-provider, and accounting numbers and explaining mismatches.
An Actual Budget user asks for a reconciliation workflow that infers principal versus interest from balances because imported payment data lacks the necessary split.

recurrence: Both 2026 requests center on incomplete financial exports: totals are available but the explanation for a difference is not, creating repeated manual reconciliation work.
current_workaround: Export CSVs from Shopify/Stripe/bank systems, combine them in spreadsheets, and leave a manual memo trail for an accountant.
incumbents_and_gap: A2X, Link My Books, QuickBooks, Xero, and enterprise reconciliation systems automate accounting at a cost. A focused local explainer for one payout batch and its evidence trail is underserved.
smallest_useful_product: An offline web app that imports three CSVs (orders/events, payout, bank), applies transparent matching rules, shows fees/refunds/timing differences as a waterfall, and exports a reconciler CSV plus accountant handoff PDF. Non-goals: direct bank/Shopify connections, bookkeeping ledger, tax advice, or auto-posting journal entries.
success_measure: On a labelled pilot dataset, users explain at least 95% of payout-to-bank variance and produce a handoff package in under 20 minutes per payout period.
monetization: one-time — CSV-based reconciliation is a concrete utility that should not require uploading financial records or a recurring integration fee.
constraints: All financial data stays local; require user-mapped columns and visible rules; no accounting/tax claims; retain currency/date precision and audit trail.
why_distinct: It explains and hands off a single reconciliation rather than trying to replace accounting software or hide matching logic behind automation.
